steps.prompt: Is the person unconscious, unable to swallow, or having a seizure?

options.label: No — conscious and able to swallow

steps.prompt: Call emergency services immediately. Do not give anything by mouth. Place in recovery position if unconscious but breathing. If trained and a glucagon kit is available, use it as instructed.
steps.cta: Call emergency services — do not give anything by mouth

steps.prompt: When in doubt, treat as low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) — giving sugar will help this and does little harm if blood sugar is actually high. Give a fast-acting sugary food or drink: 15–20 g of glucose (e.g. 4–5 glucose tablets, 150 ml fruit juice, or 5–6 regular jelly beans).
Wait 15 minutes. Is the person improving — more alert, less confused?

options.label: No — not improving or getting worse

steps.prompt: Call emergency services. Repeat the sugary drink/snack if they are still able to swallow safely. Do not leave them alone.

Once improved, give a longer-acting carbohydrate snack such as a sandwich, crackers, or a glass of milk. Encourage them to check their blood sugar if they have a meter. The person should contact their diabetes care team.
steps.cta: Give a slow-release snack and advise follow-up with their care team
